note: Which ground plate each duty stands on, and how each plate is drawn. Read by tools/ui_debug/generate_placement_sheet.py and generate_duty_sow.py. The plates themselves live in ui/assets-gothic/grounds/ and are DISCOVERED -- what art exists is a fact about the folder, so nothing here lists them. What is decided, and therefore written down, is which duty gets which, and how each one is toned down to sit under sculpts rather than compete with them.
layer_note: A ground is a layer, not a tile face. The duty-tiles tree holds the opaque face of the wheel; a plate is a transparent cut-out drawn ON TOP of that face and UNDER the figures, so the same plate can sit on any face and a face can change without redrawing its ground.
by_duty_note: Keyed by duty slug rather than by compass position, because duty tiles can be shuffled by a scenario and a ground belongs to the duty rather than to the place it happens to sit this game. Assigned in the placement sheet's wheel view and saved from it; the sow plays on the result. Both pages resolve a duty to its plate through dutyGroundFor() in tools/ui_debug/duty_sculpt_rules.js, so there is no second answer to drift from this one.

camera.why: its own outline cannot give a camera and its measuring ring can. ground_ellipse fits an ellipse; this plate is a ragged patch of plank ends, and the fit visibly misses -- it bulges past the timber on one side and falls inside it on the other, reading 30.66. The ring drawn on the source image IS a circle and fits at 31.14. The two agree to 0.48, inside the 1.5 agreement bar, so the plate is sound and the ring is the better of its two numbers. FIRST RECORDED AT 31.57 AND CORRECTED THE SAME DAY: that came from filling the ring and taking its bounding box, which measures the ring's OUTER edge and so reports a steeper camera than the ring was drawn at. Measured against rings of known centreline the old method erred by up to +0.70 degrees, more than the whole tolerance a plate is held to. The ring was stripped when the art was filed, so for a year and a day this could not be re-derived from anything committed -- which is the whole reason it is written down here. RECOVERED 2026-09-24: the ring-bearing generation was downloaded again from the session that produced it and is filed at grounds/candidates/planks_rough_ringed.png. ring_ellipse re-derives 31.1400 from it, and stripping its ring and cropping to ink reproduces grounds/planks_rough.png byte for byte, so the identity is proven rather than assumed. The number is a measurement again, not testimony
camera.method: least-squares ellipse fit to the ring's pixels

correction.why:
THIS PLATE PASSES THE WINDOW BECAUSE IT WAS SCALED UNTIL IT DID, and that is a different kind of fact from a plate that arrived inside it. It is recorded so the window can still be read honestly: a corrected plate is not evidence about where the generator puts a camera, and if the whole set ever became corrected plates the window would have stopped describing anything. Generated at 34.13 by its own outline, which is 2.6 degrees above target and outside the window; a vertical scale of 0.932476 brings it to 31.55. Flat mosaic and low rubble, so the 7 per cent squash has no visible face to distort.

THE RING THAT ARRIVED ON IT WAS NOT USED. It fits 37.19, three degrees above the tile's own outline, and correcting by it would have left the plate reading 28.80 -- 2.76 degrees from the painted sculpts' base discs, where the outline left it 0.006 away. This is the jig-measures-itself failure already on record from the first ringed cobbles batch: the ring is honest about its own geometry and can still say nothing about the tile it encircles. The ringed original is filed anyway, as the evidence for that and because the whole chain is then re-derivable -- without_ring on it gives mosaic_compass_c01.png, and correcting that reproduces this plate byte for byte.

The corroboration, and the only non-circular thing in this area: the painted sculpts' base discs are clean circles, so ground_ellipse reads them exactly, and they sit at 31.26 to 31.80 -- the ground target, from art that shares nothing with these plates. The correction moved this tile from 2.26 degrees of disagreement with the figure that stands on it to 0.006

grounds_note: All whole-number percentages. `anchor` is where down the plate's own ink the standing line falls -- where the figures' feet belong -- and it is per plate rather than global because it is a property of the picture: measured at the widest row the round rimmed plates all sit near 48%. Two plates have ever differed and both for the same reason: flagstones_slab read 61% while it was a ragged patch of loose slabs with no rim, and came back to 47.9% the day it was redrawn as a round rimmed plate; cobbles_oval reads 57.8% as of 2026-09-23 and is a ragged patch with no rim BY DESIGN. A rim is most of what sits below the equator, so a plate without one has less ink under its widest row and its anchor rises. A value far from 48 means a plate is not the same kind of object as the rest, not that it is tuned differently -- and for cobbles_oval that is the intent rather than a fault. `scale` is the plate's width as a percentage of the frame's. `dim`, `saturate` and `opacity` tone it down; the plates arrive at full strength and compete with the sculpts until they are brought down.
angle_note:
SETTLED AT 32 DEGREES, and the assignments follow it. Every duty now stands on flagstones_grey (31.5) or limestone_irregular (31.9), the two plates drawn at the board's camera; the sculpts on file measure 32.2, 32.3 and 33.5. Ground and figure are within about a degree and a half of each other, which is inside the scatter of the generator itself.

ALL FIVE PLATES NOW PASS. slate_irregular and flagstones_slab were redrawn on 2026-09-23 and read 31.1 and 32.0; cobbles_oval was redrawn the same day and reads 31.6, where the plate it replaced sat at 39.8 and had been kept as the evidence of what a mismatch looks like. That plate is now at candidates/cobbles_oval_c01.png.

THE WINDOW IS LOCKED: target 31.545, tolerance 0.48, so 31.065 to 32.025. Constants, not a formula over this folder -- a plate outside them fails rather than widening them.

They were derived once, on 2026-09-23, from the six plates then on file, every one of which had been looked at under figures and kept: slate_irregular 31.07, planks_rough 31.14, flagstones_grey 31.52, cobbles_oval 31.63, limestone_irregular 31.89, flagstones_slab 32.02 -- mean 31.545, largest deviation 0.475, and the tolerance is that rounded up to 0.48. That replaced a target of 32.0 and a tolerance of 1.0, both picked rather than measured, and which the set never centred on: five of the six sat below 32. It is about half as wide, deliberately -- against the batch that produced the current cobbles plate it admits exactly the one chosen by eye.

FOR A FEW HOURS THE WINDOW WAS THE FORMULA, recomputed from the folder, and that was wrong: a specification defined by the thing it judges has no fixed point. Simulated, filing eight plates each landing on the current ceiling moves the target +0.54 and the ceiling +1.09, every step legitimate and every suite green. Worse and less visible, filing the BEST of each batch over twelve plates walks the target DOWN from 31.55 to 31.43 while the ceiling stays pinned at 32.02 -- the highest plate anchors the top, so everything new lands below the mean and widens the window downward. The set drifts away from the sculpts one plate at a time while every step looks like tightening the standard. The tolerance was also set by a single plate, whichever sat furthest out.

CORRECTED 2026-09-24: the target was 31.55 and this note quoted a largest deviation of 0.48. The six plates' mean is 31.545 exactly, with slate_irregular and flagstones_slab sitting 0.475 either side of it. Rounding the target to two decimals moved it five thousandths toward slab and put slate at exactly 0.48 from target against a tolerance of 0.48 -- a comparison of equal decimals, which binary floating point loses by four parts in 10^16, so the plate carrying the construct duty read as 'check' on the page and failed its test. The tolerance is deliberately NOT the exact 0.475: at that value both extreme plates would sit on the boundary rather than one. Rounding the tolerance up is what gives them margin, and it is now five thousandths of a degree.

So changing the window is now a deliberate edit to two literals, asserted literally by test_the_plate_window_is_locked_and_every_plate_is_inside_it, and a plate outside it fails -- which is the moment to decide whether the plate is wrong or the family has genuinely moved.

WHAT FINALLY WORKED FOR COBBLES, after two batches that did not: attaching the plate's OWN previous art as the reference image, rather than a written description of the camera. The three batches of five measured, ring against tile outline: 32.0/35.2 mean with a 3.3 degree mean disagreement, then 29.0/28.5 with 1.5, then 32.6/33.4 with 1.1. The winner agreed to 0.1 degrees, ring 31.5 against outline 31.6.

THE RING MEASURES, IT DOES NOT STEER. Within a batch the ring's own angle is tight -- standard deviations of 0.49, 0.68 and 1.4 degrees across the three -- but between batches it moved 3 degrees on briefs asking for the same number. The generator appears to pick a camera per session and hold it, so the ring tells you whether a batch is usable and does not make it so. Expect to run more than one batch.

`default` is flagstones_grey. It was cobbles_oval, back when that was the one plate drawn from the wrong camera; it stays flagstones_grey because a fallback should point at a plate in use, and no duty stands on cobbles_oval yet.
lift_note:
How far the ground sits ABOVE the floor line, in real pixels, positive upward -- the same on all nine tiles. Set with the `lift` slider in the placement sheet's wheel view and drawn by the sow from this value.

It is not a plate's `anchor` and the two are easy to confuse. Anchor says where down a plate's own ink the standing line falls: a fact about that piece of art, measured from it, and different for every plate. Lift says how far the whole ground sits off the floor line on the tile: a fact about the tile's layout, the same for every plate, and tuned against the parchment underneath. Move a plate up with its anchor and you have told the tool the picture is wrong; move it with the lift and you have told it the board is.

One number rather than nine because the reason to lift is the banner, and every tile has the same banner geometry. The sheet reports the clearance on the WORST plate in use, not the one under the tile you clicked -- lifting until the tile in front of you is clear while another duty's taller plate still overlaps is the failure this is meant to prevent.

Real pixels, like spread, set-back, rank gap and frame.drop, because the plate is sized in frame space (`scale` is a percentage of the frame's width) and the frame is real pixels. The banner is NOT: it scales with the cell, so the clearance the sheet reports moves with the window while the lift does not.
transparency_note: How much of the ground has gone, 0-100, 0 being solid. ONE NUMBER FOR EVERY PLATE ON EVERY SCULPT SET, beside `lift` and for the same reason: both are facts about how the board is drawn rather than about one piece of art. It was a per-plate `opacity` until 2026-09-26, which made it per SET as well the moment a set carried plate rows of its own -- the two tuned sets kept 100 while every set inheriting the base went to 50, so the sow page's dropdown offered two of its own played sets at different transparencies with nothing on screen to say why. Stored as transparency rather than opacity because that is the way round it gets talked about, and because a top-level `opacity` beside a per-plate one would be two keys of a single name.
camera_note:
A PLATE MAY CARRY ITS OWN CAMERA under `grounds.<name>.camera`, and most do not. A round rimmed plate's outline IS an ellipse, so ground_ellipse measures it directly and nothing needs recording. A ragged patch is not an ellipse, and the fit is a best guess at a shape that has none -- so where a plate was generated with a measuring ring, the ring's reading is recorded here and the asset page reports it as that plate's angle.

The measured outline is still shown beside it and is never replaced. A recorded number is exactly the kind of thing that rots, so it is guarded three ways. The first two have always applied. One refuses a recorded camera further than 1.5 degrees from the plate's own outline -- that is the same bar a candidate's ring and outline must agree within, and a plate failing it should never have been filed. The second refuses a recorded camera that does not say where it came from. The third was only possible from 2026-09-24: the ring-bearing generation must be ON FILE, named by `ring_source`, and the ring must still re-derive the recorded angle. Before that the ring was discarded as a jig once the art was stripped, which is right for a plate whose outline can be measured and wrong for one carrying a recorded camera, where the ring IS the measurement -- planks_rough's original was recovered only because its generating session could still be found.

planks_rough is the first and so far only plate with one.

per_set_note: How one sculpt set stands its plates. The plate ART is the same whatever size the sculpts are; how it is STOOD is not -- `lift` is a distance in real pixels between the floor line and the ground, and `scale` sizes the plate against figures that are 90 px tall in one set and 210 in another. A set may restand one plate and leave the others alone; each plate's row is merged on its own and is a whole row. `by_duty` is deliberately not splittable: which duty stands on which plate is a fact about the board, and letting it split would put one duty on two different grounds depending on which sculpts were loaded. The 210_painted anchors here were tuned on 2026-09-25 and landed in the base slot by mistake.
